etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English jargoun, jargon, from Old French jargon, a variant of gargon, gargun (“chatter; talk; language”).
senses: (uncountable) A technical terminology unique to a particular subject.
(countable) A language characteristic of a particular group.
To utter jargon; to emit confused or unintelligible sounds.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: Alternative form of jargoon (“A variety of zircon”).
